attempts.summary: Joined node2's and node3's separate segments off node1 into a single transparent L2 domain: on node1 (SONiC) created bridge br1 with eth1 (facing node2) and eth2 (facing node3) as members, no IP on br1. Assigned node2 eth1=192.168.50.11/24 and node3 eth1=192.168.50.12/24 via nmcli (persisted as ONBOOT=yes ifcfg files). Verified direct L2 reachability (ping TTL=64, unchanged — proving no routing hop) and confirmed node1's bridge FDB dynamically learned both peer MACs on their respective bridge ports, i.e. node1 forwards frames rather than routing. Persisted the bridge across reboots via a new systemd oneshot unit (br1-setup.service, enabled, WantedBy=multi-user.target) since SONiC's live kernel bridge state would otherwise not survive a restart. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id/boot-time baselines, rebooted each node individually (node1 then node2 then node3), polled until exec was available again, confirmed a different boot_id/boot-time on each, and verified post-restart that the bridge/interfaces/services and node2↔node3 L2 connectivity fully recovered before moving to the next node.
